scenes.headline: How a bidirectional encoder reads the whole sentence
scenes.sub: BERT: full attention, hidden tokens, and one vector per token
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Filbert! BERT reads every token with the whole sentence in view. Here's how.

scenes.text: Take the causal mask off, so every token sees both sides. Then hide 15% of the tokens and train the model to fill them in.
scenes.say: Take the causal mask off, so every token sees both sides. Then hide fifteen percent of the tokens, and train the model to put them back.

steps.label: A decoder: each token sees only its past
steps.say: A decoder masks the future. Each token sees only what came before it.

steps.label: An encoder: every token sees every token
steps.note: no next token to predict, so no mask
steps.say: An encoder has no next token to predict, so it keeps every pair: both sides of the context.

scenes.title: From tokens to one vector each

steps.say: Each token, its sentence and its position each pick a row from a table. The three rows are added.

steps.note: every token reads the whole sequence
steps.say: Twelve blocks of attention and MLP follow. In every block, each token reads the whole sequence.
Out comes one vector per token. At the hidden slots, a small head guesses the original word.
For a task, take the vector of the first token, called CLS, and train one new layer on it.

items.say: Pick fifteen percent of the positions at random.
Eighty percent of those become a mask token.
Ten percent become a random token.
And ten percent stay as they are.
It must predict the original at all of them, so it can't trust any token it sees.

left.title: BERT: two objectives
items: Plus: is sentence B the real next one?
left.say: BERT also guessed whether sentence B really followed sentence A. Half the time it was a random one.

right.title: RoBERTa: masks only
right.say: A careful retrain a year later dropped that task, and matched or beat BERT. Fresh masks, more data and bigger batches mattered more.

scenes.label: tokens of context in ModernBERT, sixteen times BERT's 512
scenes.say: Encoders kept improving. ModernBERT reads over eight thousand tokens, with rotary positions.

scenes.text: Seeing both sides makes an encoder a strong, cheap reader for classification and embeddings, and a poor writer.
scenes.say: Seeing both sides makes an encoder a strong, cheap reader. It's also why it can't write efficiently.

recap: Full attention: every token sees both sides
Masked tokens: hide 15%, predict them back
CLS or pooling: one vector per input
scenes.say: No mask. Hidden tokens. One vector out.
